_comment: Guided tour of the ndXplorer window. Steps point at the controls ndX drew; the awaited step waits for the user to press Contrast. The demo (Help > Guide opens it when nothing is loaded) is a burst table with three FRET populations.

steps.title: Look at many bursts at once
steps.text: ndXplorer shows a table of single-molecule bursts (or image pixels) as histograms of any two of its columns, so populations show up as clouds and you can gate them. When nothing is loaded the tour offers a small demo table with five simulated populations (Load example). You press the controls; the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Load the example
steps.text: With nothing loaded, Load example (over the empty map) opens a simulated burst table: five populations with a known FRET efficiency and stoichiometry. Every step below points at it. If a table is open already this step is done.

steps.title: Open your own data here
steps.text: File > Open and the Import entries read burst folders, CSV tables, HDF5, sampling files and ChiSurf projects; From MMFDB browses the database. A file or folder dropped on the window opens too.

steps.title: Choose what to plot
steps.text: The x and y columns of the 2-D map. A fresh table opens on a default pair; the demo shows donor lifetime against FRET efficiency, where each population lies along the static FRET line. Any numeric column can go on either axis.

steps.title: The map
steps.text: Each dense spot is a population. Drag a rectangle here to gate it: the histograms on the margins and every other plot then show only the selected bursts.

steps.title: Set the colour scale
steps.text: Counts per bin are coloured; one dense cloud can wash out the rest. Contrast sets the colour limits from the data so faint populations stay visible.

steps.title: Keep a selection
steps.text: Gates are listed under Selection: save them, load them again, or write the selected burst ids so another analysis can reuse exactly these bursts.

steps.title: Where to go next
steps.text: Help > Quick reference lists the parts of the window in a few lines.
